And we will call the witness who can prove that the footage was really made on this day and on that very route. So what I ask for the moment is that this video could be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D294 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Mikulicic, if at any later stage you come with a witness or with further details about this video, would you also, then, please bring a very, very, very, detailed map, which allows us, whenever there is an road sign to the left there, to the right there, which enables us to verify what road it approximately was, because that would certainly assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because one of the questions, if I look at some detail to the map the witness gave us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And if I zoom in on the area of Gracac --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You will see, Your Honour, in a direction of north-west the village of Ricice and after that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. Let me first try to find that. I have zoomed in extremely ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: It's a little bit on the left from Gracac, in the north-east direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, now we have a blow-up on the screen, and if you follow the red line, towards left, from Gracac, you will find the village of Ricice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And afterwards where the mark six is and a little bit on the left, the village of Rok, which is Sveti Rok.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And further on, it's Gospic, which is on top of the screen not visible for the moment in that blow-up. So that was the route that witness took on that particular day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Isn't it right, Mr. Vanderostyne?

utterances.speaker: EDMOND VANDEROSTYNE
utterances.text: It is right, to the best of my knowledge, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And now, where at the exit of Gracac, Mr. Mikulicic, you consider --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes. For that particular --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the left and right where it goes to the right to Zagreb --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I will provide a better map if you wish, Your Honour, just for your information, and that will be clearly seen on that map. If the usher could please pull up the 3D00-0387.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because my -- I'll tell you why I'm asking it. My logic tells me that if you are travelling in the direction as the witness indicated, that if you want to go to Zagreb you rather turn to the left, not to the right. But it might be a local -- but that's -- here we have Gracac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I believe -- and I'm sure you will correct me if I'm wrong, but if we replay the video, I believe the sign actually said right to Zadar, left to Zagreb. [Sic]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's replay it, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yeah. It's on the screen right now, Your Honour. I'm sorry, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm sorry -- yes, I might have did write it down, but I might have made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's to the right, to Zagreb -- yes, you're right. I did write it down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Both name it's beginning with Z, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise for taking your time with that. Then --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I think it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear myself in an echo, which is not very pleasant.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Although are you not in Switzerland.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's move on. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Your Honour. If you wish we could pull up the map --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not at this moment. First of all, I fully admit that I made a mistake here, which caused me to ask further questions. Let move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Vanderostyne, you returned to downtown Gracac, in the centre. You parked the car there and got out of the car. And then you saw a large group of uniformed men for whom you later established that they were members of the Delta unit of the Special Police. Have I understood your evidence correctly?

utterances.speaker: EDMOND VANDEROSTYNE
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You then approached an individual because you had been told that he was the commander of this unit, and you called this person a lieutenant. That's what you used in your statement, correct?

utterances.speaker: EDMOND VANDEROSTYNE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, how did you learn that this person was a lieutenant? Did he tell you, or did you find out in some other way?

utterances.speaker: EDMOND VANDEROSTYNE
utterances.text: I asked in -- so in the first place I approached a little group. It was not an individual, a little group of relaxed khaki uniforms, I will call them: The accordion player, the man with the straw hat, the man -- it was a little group. And it's at that group that I have asked rather fast, quickly, Who is your lieutenant? And he said, That man. And I then moved towards the person who -- who was said to me to be the lieutenant, the commander of the unit. That's how I understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: My question was, Did this person say that he was a lieutenant, or was it something that you actually suggested? That was the gist of my question.

utterances.speaker: EDMOND VANDEROSTYNE
utterances.text: No, sir. I asked, Who is your lieutenant? And that man, that Croatian man, directed me towards this man.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did you notice on this man's uniform any emblems or any markings showing what rank he held?

utterances.speaker: EDMOND VANDEROSTYNE
utterances.text: The only emblem I have noticed is the MUP, which he showed me himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: While you were talking with this man, this commander, your photographer was making photos. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDMOND VANDEROSTYNE
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Was he banned from taking photos? Was he forbidden or prohibited by someone?

utterances.speaker: EDMOND VANDEROSTYNE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Could we please now call up P325. It's a series of four photographs that were introduced into evidence by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, when waiting for this, I noticed, Mr. Vanderostyne, and -- that this morning you were asked or at least you said, I asked him very quickly, who is your commander? Who is in charge? And he showed me on the opposite of the street or the opposite of the square, and did I that in order to everyone should -- Your question, as you formulated it earlier today was that you asked, Who is your commander? Whereas now, you formulate your question as who is your lieutenant? Could you help us out, which words you exactly used, and --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir. I cannot 13 years later, which words I used exactly, I cannot, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So, therefore, you also -- can you tell us whether anyone confirmed if you would use the words or if you have not used the words informed you that the man in command was a lieutenant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You see, sir, Mr. President, the unit I observed was -- had the kind of size of -- of what -- what I would call a company, a company's 100 men, military or paramilitary unit. At the command of a company is a lieutenant or a captain, but he is the commander, he is in charge, and that was the meaning of my question to one subordinate, one common -- not an army man but one policemen of that unit who is in charge, who can I speak to, who is responsible guy, who is -- who can -- it's not just a small talk I had to -- small questions I had to ask. I wanted someone who was in charge, whether he is a lieutenant or a captain or whether those uniformed people had -- had -- had rank insignia. I can imagine that special troops have no rank insignia, but that was not my focus. I wanted someone who was in charge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Let's take a look at this photo, Mr. Vanderostyne. Would you agree with me that these two uniformed individuals are actually posing for your photographer?

utterances.speaker: EDMOND VANDEROSTYNE
utterances.text: Whether they are posing, sir, is an interpretation, and you can read that picture in several ways. What I read in it is that they are relaxed, so they are part. I explained that there are two groups. One group was -- was looting; one group was relaxed, drinking wine, playing accordion, cutting hair, and so on. Are they posing for the photographer? In my view, they are not. It is a kind of relaxed attitude of -- of men that have finished, that have completed operation. That is my interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: In the upper right-hand corner of the photograph, you can see the yellow bus. Did you ask the commander, the person that you talked with, what they were actually doing here and what was that bus going to be used for?

utterances.speaker: EDMOND VANDEROSTYNE
utterances.text: There was -- those are two questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [In English] Sorry. Just one after another.

utterances.speaker: EDMOND VANDEROSTYNE
utterances.text: I did ask the commander or that person what his unit was doing, and he -- he answered, to make the city vrij, so that is a combination of English and German that I have literally -- that you will see in that notebook. What are you doing, what is your unit doing, what is your mission to make this city vrij? So that's is an indication to me that I spoke English and German one through another. Your other question is, did I ask that person what that bus was for. It is possible. It's possible. Anyway, I'm sure, and that's in my notebook, that person said our job is almost completed, which means, in my opinion, we're going back home.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you aware or do you know what was in this yellow building behind the bus? What was the purpose of that building at the time when you arrived at Gracac? If I were to tell you, Mr. Vanderostyne, that this was the logistics staff of the Special Police in Gracac, would that refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: EDMOND VANDEROSTYNE
utterances.text: No, I have no -- I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I did not hear the answer to the question when it was still put as an open question. When you were asked what was the purpose of that building at the time when you arrived Gracac, what answer did you give?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Mr. Mikulicic, on the record we see a first question, whether you know; and then there's no answer. And then Mr. Mikulicic is on the record continuing by saying, "if I were to tell you, Mr. Vanderostyne." But, Mr. Mikulicic, have you waited for an answer? Have you received an answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I think I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and that's not on the record. That's the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, you're --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: No, I should check --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't have to apologize for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I should check the transcript before I pose another question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I also did not hear any answer translated to us. May I take it that your answer, that did you not know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly. I do not know, I did not know what the purpose of that being was for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and then -- that's clear. That is now on the record. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now ask the registry to show us P324, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the photograph to appear on the screen, Mr. Vanderostyne, you said a number of times how uniformed persons were looting in Gracac. Did you see that yourself, personally?

utterances.speaker: EDMOND VANDEROSTYNE
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Can you describe to us when you saw this? What were the circumstances?

utterances.speaker: EDMOND VANDEROSTYNE
utterances.text: I saw it at least two occasions. First was when I entered Gracac, so that was in -- at the outskirts. What I call the outskirts is when I entered at the right-hand side of the road. When I entered I saw policemen, so I'm speaking about grey -- grey/blue uniforms, policemen, taking booty, looting, looting houses at the outskirts. I saw police vehicles being loaded with booty, and there were civilian trucks being loaded -- loaded, as well, at that -- in that precise spot. There was also burning, but that is not your question, I understand. I saw also looting by khaki uniform in -- in and around the city square, centre square, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Can you describe to us what war booty is. What kind of items are that, according to what you saw?

utterances.speaker: EDMOND VANDEROSTYNE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I can only refer to -- to -- to those notes. I have --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: EDMOND VANDEROSTYNE
utterances.text: Well, if you allow me. It's -- of course, it's examples and I -- you may well understand, sir, I do not know -- I do not write every single experience, but what I have written about the centre of -- of Gracac and in particular about the blue -- blue -- blue truck with the Cyrillic letters is hifi television, shoes, bags, and suitcases.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: When you're talking about the blue truck, is it this truck that we see on the photograph and you also see it in front of you on the monitor?

utterances.speaker: EDMOND VANDEROSTYNE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... so, but I rely on my notes, and that's what I have seen, and I'm sure, I am sure; I am standing with that, whether that is the same. I see a blue truck, and I see khaki uniform, and I see one carrying something that seems to be a television set or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: That is my next question, Mr. Vanderostyne. This object that this person is obviously holding, is it a document box, or is it a TV set, or is it something else? Did you personally see this?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is a matter to place before the Trial Chamber in -- the witness has clearly testified as to what it seems like. He is just submitted the photograph, and I think the matter now before Trial Chamber to make an interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There are two different matters. The first one is what the witness saw, and I think he has clearly explained that; and the second issue is whether he saw the scene which is photographed or that his answers to what he had seen refers to -- although nearby, same village, but -- So when you said relying on your notes you saw TVs being looted, hifi TVs, were you referring to what we see at the photograph now, or is it ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. President, sir, I rely on my notes and my notes on Gracac, on the -- that central square, and that is readable, I think, is a blue truck with Cyrillic letters is being loaded with hifi televisions, shoes, bags and suitcases, and I have written next to it, and that's, of course, my own interpretation, war booty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I can follow that because I can read your Dutch. It is actually in the little booklet, the second one. So relying on your notes, do you now think that you described what you see on this picture, or was it -- might have been another blue car, or don't you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That picture is definitely taken in Gracac centre. However, sir, the photographer has -- I was not always next to him, as I explained. He has taken pictures on the central square itself and in a -- in a side road of the central square. I was not present in that side road of the central square, but I have seen, I did see a blue truck with -- et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Might be the same; might be another one than the one on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, does that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You personally did not see this person stealing a television set and treating it as war booty. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDMOND VANDEROSTYNE
utterances.text: No. I mean, I did see it myself, of course, because that is what I have written that afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderostyne, let's look at the two persons who are on the left side of the photograph. Can you recognize who these persons are? Are these persons wearing uniforms, or are they civilians?

utterances.speaker: EDMOND VANDEROSTYNE
utterances.text: I agree that this -- these -- this is not very clear, just as the President has said earlier in the session. I don't know. And again, I'm not sure that I have witnessed that exactly scene, that picture. I was not always next to the -- by the contrary, I was not always next to the photographer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we know show a photograph of this truck, marked 9980. I don't know exactly where it is in this sequence of photographs, but it is marked 9980. I assume that it's the next one.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. I selected only the four relevant prints. 9980 is not part of the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [In English] Okay. Could I then ask the usher to blow up this picture. That's the one. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, even if you didn't use it, is it uploaded, this photograph, in e-court so that we're not --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I don't believe so, Mr. President. I think these photographs in fact were uploaded separately. They were given separate 65 ter numbers previously and then amalgamated into one exhibit form. So I don't think -- if I may have a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are these photographs anywhere available in --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: It is, Mr. President. It is available electronically, but I don't know if it has been released. I think there is a system there -- may I just have a minute, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you could please try to assist us, and meanwhile, Mr. Mikulicic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the photograph, we will be seeing actually also the other side, the left side of the vehicle. I would just like to point out to you that this large sign in the middle of the truck written in Cyrillic, in the Cyrillic script, is actually street sign. This is not a registration plate, a vehicle licence plate. It's a street sign?

utterances.speaker: EDMOND VANDEROSTYNE
utterances.text: Might well be.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did you see signs like this on houses in Gracac or anywhere where you were passing through?

utterances.speaker: EDMOND VANDEROSTYNE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... street signs in Cyrillic letters. I cannot recall. Probably -- probably yes. I would be -- I would be surprised if there were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [In English] Mr. Usher, could we see this photo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could it be that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: It's written in Cyrillic Ulica Nemanjina, as far as I understand the Cyrillic letters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this is a photograph of that same truck. Mr. Vanderostyne, I would like to draw your attention to the front left part of the truck where you can see the registration sign. It's a licence plate indicating a police vehicle. Can you please tell us if you saw such licence plates on vehicles -- on other vehicles as you were travelling through that area in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: EDMOND VANDEROSTYNE
utterances.text: No, sir, I cannot. Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this photograph, please, and I hope that Ms. Mahindaratne will be able to assist us by providing the electronic number of this item.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, but we would need a little bit of time, not immediately. I have asked that it be released, but it takes a little while to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but you have located it and you're in a position to upload it into e-court so that it can be electronically --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Mr. Registrar, the photograph of a blue truck but now taken a little bit more from the left-hand side and including a licence plate would be number ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D295, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D295. And we will wait with a decision, but there's no objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is no objection, so once it is -- that's admitted into evidence but subject to being electronically uploaded in the system.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if that doesn't happen in the course of this session that -- I just want to indicate it might not happen before the break, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take that this is an administrative matter rather than anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [In English] Could I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The only thing, Mr. Mikulicic, that comes into my mind is -- is the following. Of course, the witness could not confirm that it is a police registration number, but what -- let's just assume that on the -- that this is a police vehicle. What is the Chamber supposed to -- to understand from this? That -- I mean, I can -- just two options. One would the police is in the exercise of its legal functions, that is perhaps is there an order to seize or -- other option would that the police is involved in looting. I mean, these are two extremes. But it's unclear to me how we have to understand this and what was on your mind when you asked these questions and when you showed these photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my position is this. What the witness saw was the preparation of the unit of the Special Police to leave Gracac after they had completed their assignment on the front, after the logis -- they were loading their equipment from the logistics staff into their truck, including computers, televisions, documents, and other equipment. What the witness saw, he actually interpreted during those 15 minutes that he spent in Gracac as looting, and actually that is not what it as.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, at least it's your position that is not what it was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, when they were packing and moving back home there would have been no reason for being aggressive against the photographer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Although no question was asked to you, Mr. Vanderostyne --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I understand that you -- Please proceed, Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. On the basis of this response that the witness gave us, my next question -- unfortunately we don't have any more of -- of the photograph on the monitor, but the person that is next to the truck is actually looking at the photographer and they are smiling. They don't seem to be aggressive in any way. They are actually -- it seems or it appears that they're actually posing. Perhaps we can put the photograph back on the monitor for the witness to look at it again.

utterances.speaker: EDMOND VANDEROSTYNE
utterances.text: There is no need. I can answer that, Mr. President, and in fact, I have done already so earlier in this session. I have seen that in other war situations, as well, there is a kind of -- it's exactly -- it's correct what -- what Mr. Defence is saying. This is not an aggressive posture at that time, and I have seen that, noticed that in other war -- war situations, very much so. There's a kind of pride or proud -- excuse me. People feel proud --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [In English] I'm sorry to interrupt you, Mr. Vanderostyne --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... Mr. President, I think the witness is answering.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't ask the witness for his conclusions. I didn't ask him to compare the wars all over the world because all we know is that each war is different from another war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Each war is different. At the same time, Mr. Mikulicic, of course, you are -- where the witness clearly testified that hifi TVs, shoes, other items --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And the big bags.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, bags but also other matters, that where he testified that you more or less wanted him to conclude that the context was such that it was not looting. Of course, there's some element of conclusion in looting. There's some element of conclusion in not looting. I mean, that -- it is all -- as the witness clearly explained, he interprets what he has seen, and he earlier said -- and the reference to other war situations was only marginal because earlier he said that he noticed at the time not in other wars but here that they apparently took some pride in what was happening, and then he was certainly not referring to any other war situation. The only thing he now added that such an attitude appears to him familiar, having been in other war situations. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Vanderostyne, before the Operation Storm, were you ever on the territory of the so-called Republic of Serbian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: EDMOND VANDEROSTYNE
utterances.text: Before -- before the Operation Storm, well, I -- I had been, sir, in Baranja which I was formerly part of republic of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: With all due respect, Mr. Vanderostyne, Baranja is in a completely different part of the Republic of Croatia, to the east. We're talking about the southern part. So my question was whether you were in that southern area around Knin, before the Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: EDMOND VANDEROSTYNE
utterances.text: In the Krajina part of -- well, Krajina republic -- what the Serbs called Republic of Krajina I think -- I had not been before, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Before that time, were you familiar with the tasks, positions, and functions of the Special Police of the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: EDMOND VANDEROSTYNE
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Were you aware what the assignment of the Special Police was in Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: EDMOND VANDEROSTYNE
utterances.text: No, not at all, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [In English] Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions. That concludes my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Mikulicic, other counsel have indicated that they would have no questions. Does that remain still your position? Yes. Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I have just one question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderostyne, you were shown a picture -- that picture where a person was seen loading the blue vehicle with something square, and there were two persons in the background.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour. I must object, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: It is not clearly from the picture whether this person is loading or unloading the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President. That's not -- that wasn't the question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. But nevertheless, a person.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Carrying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- carrying -- whether loading or unloading with but in a movement which suggests that at least that object is put in or put out of that truck -- yes, you have been shown a photo in which the square object was handled this way close to this truck, yes, and then your question, Ms. Mahindaratne, would be?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And there were two other persons in the background, and you were asked about their attire. Now, on 8 August, do you recall seeing any civilians in the Gracac town; do you recall?

utterances.speaker: EDMOND VANDEROSTYNE
utterances.text: I have seen civilians in -- at the outskirts of Gracac, working together or close by those grey/blue uniformed police.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderostyne, my question, was Gracac town where you saw the khaki-attired men?

utterances.speaker: EDMOND VANDEROSTYNE
utterances.text: No, madam, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: That is all, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one question for you about this bus. It was not entirely clear what this bus was for. The job was almost done, would they return home apparently somewhere else? It was not fully clear to me what you told us that you understood at that time, the bus was for.

utterances.speaker: EDMOND VANDEROSTYNE
utterances.text: What I understood, sir, is definitely that that bus would take that unit back to their area of origin, Vinkovci.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: EDMOND VANDEROSTYNE
utterances.text: That is sure definitely what I understood at that time, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The bus was waiting for them once finished to take them back to --

utterances.speaker: EDMOND VANDEROSTYNE
utterances.text: That was my interpretation -- well, it was my interpretation, or someone has told me so, but that was definitely what I understood, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. And I have a small question for you, Mr. Mikulicic. The witness said that he thought that the place where he had been was formerly part of the republic of Serbian Krajina, which of course was not just Sector South or Sector North, you had also other sectors, where you said that that was not what you asked for. Is it that you contest that where the witness had been was part of Serbian Krajina, or that you --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, you're not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I'm just contesting whether even Slavonia was part of the Krajina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but of course your question was -- you more or less blamed the witness for --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and you said -- I asked you what you asked him. I think he answered that perfectly right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that has been clarified now as well. Then since there appear to be no questions -- Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I have two points of order, I guess. To correct the transcript at page 51, we had, as you will recall, a discussion about that sign as to where to turn to Zagreb and to Zadar. I believe the transcript should say that the sign says Zagreb is to the left and Zadar is to the right. Just so that the record is clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters kindly ask that all microphones which are not in use be switched off. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least as matters stand now, whatever's on the transcript is that the traffic sign indicates at a junction that to the right it is Zadar, and to the left it's Zagreb, and there's no straight on indication.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. My second point is just to note for the record that we now have the notes of the witness. We are going through them. We will endeavour to -- if there is anything that comes up to resolve it by agreement with the Prosecution so as to avoid the need of the witness having to come back to address the issue. However, I wanted to note that obviously there is a possibility that something could come up, and I wanted to preserve our position on that in terms of going to the Chamber and asking if needed to come back to that point, but I'm fully aware that our efforts are to work with the Prosecution to see if we can come to agreement to make that unnecessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is on the record, and may I take it that this is valid for all parties. Well, perhaps not for the Prosecution because you, Ms. Mahindaratne, you said that there was no need -- you never asked for it, whereas Mr. Misetic apparently is interested in this.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time, Mr. Misetic, if there is any reason to revisit these notes, then of course, the Prosecution who considered them not necessary at this moment then may change its mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, our position is very much the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then -- and I take it that is true for the Cermak Defence as well. Then I have to -- I would suggest that if the parties are interested to see the original, that the witness is now still here, they perhaps just have a glance in it unless they say, Well, that is not very important for us because then I would leave the originals in the hands of the witness. Mr. Vanderostyne, keep them well in case they ever might be needed. Then I also noticed that since the copying is one-sided, that it might not be easy to identify exactly what is on the right pages and what's is on the left page. For copying, I instructed that empty pages, and there quite a number of empty pages in the booklet, that they are not copied because the pages are not numbered. I, however, asked that the sequence of the pages would be unaffected during copying, so I've got one with a staple on it, the other one not. Therefore, everyone should take care that we -- we leave them in the sequence as they are now. Mr. Vanderostyne, this concludes your testimony in this Court. I'd like to thank you very much for having answered all the questions, and I wish you a safe trip home again. Mr. Usher, could you escort Mr. Vanderostyne out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi, or Ms. Mahindaratne, I do understand that you have not your next witness stand by.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. General Forand will start tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Will start tomorrow morning. It's always -- we lose another hour in court, but matters are as they are. Then if there is no other procedural issue to be raised at this moment, and I do not see anyone jumping up. We'll resume at -- yes, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry. Let me take the opportunity if we have some extra time. There is one issue that came up today that I didn't raise an objection, but just something for the consideration of the Trial Chamber and the Prosecution. There were badges shown to the witness, and I think it came up once before with a previous witness regarding a Puma badge. The Court will recall we had a prior discussion about photo IDs with witnesses, and just as a point in the future, I'm not sure how the Chamber wishes to proceed as a matter of procedure, if badges are going to be shown to Prosecution witnesses, it might be appropriate to give them a lineup of different badges and see if they can select them rather than showing them one and saying, is this the Puma badge or is this a Special Police badge or whatever the case may be. I think the principles are consistent with what we discussed earlier with regard to photo lineups. It's a new issue that's raised. I don't know how the Chamber wishes -- whether in writing, et cetera, but it came up today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is a kind of an emblem lineup and also identification but then for emblems rather than --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: We'll take note of it, Mr. President. I just want to point out, of course, with regard to the badge that the witness identified. It was clear in fact on the photographs of -- photographs taken on 8 August in Gracac that what he identified in court was exactly that, the MUP -- you know, the letters MUP, policija.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That of course -- there is a slight difference if -- if a photograph has been taken. If a witness describes an emblem where there is no picture available from what he saw at that time, then of course it makes more sense to make also Oslo emblem confrontation then if there is a photograph, if he has described it because it is not just a picture of the emblem, but it is a picture of an emblem which was photographed on the same location on the same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Just two points. My colleague advises me that actually the emblem was not identical to the one that was in the picture because there was a lightning -- he didn't recognise the lightning bolt, and the second is, I wonder --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nevertheless, he didn't recognise it. I fully agree with you. But I think that this picture was shown to the witness on the basis of what was found on the photograph. But I do agree with you that it needed some further interpretation whether it was upside down or the other way around.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Be that as it may, though, in the future if we are going to go through that process, I would just note for the record that we would from now on ask that the witnesses not be shown one badge and then asked, Is this is the Puma badge or whatever the case might be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we compare the technique used during Oslo confrontations, you usually find other persons, similar size, similar et cetera. I do not whether emblems, similar size, similar colours, et cetera, should be created for those persons or whether they do exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: There are plenty of badges as I'm sure the Prosecution has most if not all of them. The issue is in most of these statements or many of these statements, I should say, Your Honour, the witnesses often say I don't know, I don't recall it was a 7 or whether it was a 4, et cetera, and to have the Prosecution even inadvertently say, Is this the badge of the Puma Brigade, it suggests to the witness that it is and therefore --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I do agree with you, and I think I made that clear already that to the extent possible, especially where there are no photographs taken at that same day, that the witness be shown a series of emblems so that he can -- that does not just one for him to recognise, to identify, but that he must make a choice or say that none of them resembles what he saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it reminds me when asking you about procedural matters that I have still one -- not a decision but the reasons for a decision. That is the chamber's reasons for granting trial-related protective measures for Witness 54. On the 13th of May, 2008, the Prosecution requested the Chamber to order the trial-related protective measures of pseudonym and face distortion for Witness 54. This request can be found in the transcript, beginning at page 2767. On the same day, the Cermak Defence and the Markac Defence indicated that they did not object to the motion. On the 14th of May, 2008, the Gotovina Defence stated that it did not oppose the motion. And, on the same day, the Chamber granted the motion with reasons to follow as indicated on transcript page 2773. On the 1st of May, 2008, the Chamber held in its reasons for its first protective measures decision in this case that the party seeking protective measures for a witness must demonstrate an objectively grounded risk to the security or welfare of the witness or the witness's family, should it become known that the witness has given evidence before the Tribunal. The mere expression of fear by a witness is insufficient to justify protective measures. This standard can be satisfied by showing, for example, that a threat was made against the witness or the witness's family. Witness 54, a Croatian Serb, and his family live in Croatia where he also owns property. The Chamber found that the expected testimony of Witness 54 could antagonise certain persons in the place where he and his family live. The witness stated that he is repeatedly discriminated against because of his ethnicity and that his property in Croatia was repeatedly damaged. The Chamber additionally considered the fact that the Defence did not object to the request and that the public's ability to follow the proceedings would not be hindered by the assignment of a pseudonym to the witness and face distortion on the television broadcast. For the aforementioned reasons, the Chamber found that the Prosecution has demonstrated an objectively grounded risk to the security and welfare of Witness 54, should it become known that he has given evidence before the Tribunal that is sufficient to warrant the granting of the requested protective measures. This concludes the Chamber's reasons for its decision to grant protective measures for Witness 54. We adjourn, and we'll resume tomorrow, the 3rd of June, 9.00, Courtroom I.
